source.title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory

accepted.question_text: How can one determine the minimal possible order of a representation for a given phase-type distribution? Here a phase-type distribution is the distribution of the absorption time in a finite-state absorbing Markov chain; a representation is the underlying Markov chain data, and its order is the number of transient states, equivalently the dimension of the generator matrix T. Given the Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=p(s)/q(s) of the probability density, with p and q coprime and deg q called the degree of the distribution, characterize or compute the smallest number of transient states among all phase-type representations of the same distribution.

evidence.quote: In particular the problem of finding the minimal order of a representation for a given PH distribution is still open.
The order of a representation is the number of transient states of the Markov chain which is the dimension of the matrix T.
The general problem of finding a minimal representation for a given PH-distribution is still open

accepted.question_text: How can phase-type distributions be characterized using only the Laplace transform of their probability density? A phase-type distribution is an absorption-time distribution for a finite-state absorbing Markov chain. The known characterization cited in the source says that a nonzero distribution on [0,infinity) is phase-type exactly when it has a rational Laplace transform with a unique pole of maximal real part and its probability density is positive on [0,infinity); the open problem is to replace this mixed s-domain and t-domain criterion by a condition stated solely in terms of the Laplace transform.

evidence.quote: The characterization given by the theorem is simple but one may regret that it is expressed partly in the t-domain and partly in the s-domain.
Problem 1: Find a characterization of PH-distributions only in terms of their Laplace transform.

accepted.question_text: What is the representational power of feedback Cox representations for phase-type distributions? A Cox representation is a phase-type representation obtained from a series of exponential stages by allowing direct routing to the absorbing state after a stage; a feedback Cox representation is obtained by adding feedbacks to this Cox structure. Determine which phase-type distributions can be represented by feedback Cox representations, and whether there is a cyclic analogue of the theorem that every triangular phase-type representation is equivalent to an ordered Cox representation of no larger order.

evidence.quote: A generalization of the previous form, by allowing a direct routing to the absorbing state after leaving a given state, results in the Cox representation
A new type of representation can also be obtained by adding feedbacks to the Cox representation. It is called the feedback Cox.
Problem 2: Investigate the power of representation of the feedback Cox representations.

accepted.question_text: What general properties can be proved about the zero locations, or the relative pole and zero locations, of the Laplace transform of a phase-type distribution? The setting is the Laplace transform of the probability density of a phase-type distribution; known eigenvalue results constrain possible pole locations because poles of the transform are eigenvalues of the generator matrix T in any phase-type representation, but the analogous general information about zeros remains unknown.

evidence.quote: Since the poles of the Laplace transform of the distribution are eigenvalues of the T matrix of any representation
Problem 3: Find general properties about the zero location, or the relative pole/zero location, of the Laplace transform of a PH-distribution.

accepted.question_text: What is a natural direct counterpart of reachability for phase-type representations? In a phase-type representation, a generator T is called simple when any two distinct initial probability distributions give rise to two distinct phase-type distributions, and this simplicity is close to observability through a rank condition on the matrix [v, Tv, ..., T^(n-1)v]. The problem is to identify the corresponding reachability notion for phase-type representations in a way that has a natural probabilistic, structural, or graph-theoretic interpretation rather than only an indirect dual-time construction.

evidence.quote: Definition 2 (O'Cinneide 1989): A PH generator T is simple if any two initial probability distributions α1 ≠ α2, give rise to two different PH-distributions.
This notion is very close to our observability notion. Up to now, a direct counterpart of reachability is not known.
Problem 4: Give a natural interpretation of the counterpart of reachability for PH-representations

accepted.question_text: For phase-type distributions with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s), where q(s)=(1+s/c)(1+s/(a+ib))(1+s/(a-ib)) and a,b,c are positive real parameters, suppose the eigenvalue-angle condition for phase-type generators gives a lower bound n_min on the possible order of any representation. Does there always exist a phase-type representation of exactly order n_min for every such distribution?
accepted.context_brief: Minimal order for one real and one complex pole pair

evidence.quote: Consider a PH-distribution with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s), q(s)=(1+s/c)(1+s/(a+ib))(1+s/(a-ib)) where a, b, c > 0.
For PH-distributions with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s) where q(s) is as in (42), Theorem 6 gives a minimal order nmin for a representation.
Conjecture 1: There exists a representation of order nmin for such a distribution.

accepted.question_text: For a phase-type distribution whose Laplace transform is f_tilde(s)=p(s)/q(s), with p and q coprime, deg p=2, and deg q=3, what necessary and sufficient conditions guarantee that the distribution has a phase-type representation with exactly three transient states? The question is to go beyond the known order-three condition for the special reciprocal cubic case with one real pole and one complex-conjugate pole pair.

evidence.quote: A more interesting problem, both from the theoretical and practical points of view, would be the characterization of order 3 PH-distributions.

Problem 5: Consider a PH-distribution whose Laplace transform is f_tilde(s)=p(s)/q(s), where p(s) has degree two and q(s) degree three. Under which conditions (besides condition (43)) has this distribution an order 3 representation?

accepted.question_text: How is cyclicity in the directed graph of a phase-type representation related to the occurrence of non-real poles in the Laplace transform of the associated phase-type distribution? Characterize when cyclicity is compulsory, when a distribution with real poles can nevertheless have a natural or smaller cyclic representation, and whether cyclic representations can have smaller order than every acyclic representation of the same distribution.

evidence.quote: In some cases the cyclicity is compulsory, that is when the Laplace transform of the distribution has non-real poles.
But in some cases there may exist cyclic representations which may be of a smaller order than any acyclic one.
From this discussion it appears that the relation between the cyclicity of the representation and the existence of non-real poles is not yet fully understood.

needs_review.question_text_raw: what is really a good practical representation?

evidence.quote: Comparing the respective benefits of the incompatible goals of low order and triangular form raises the question: what is really a good practical representation?
